text: Thenar pays people to record robot arm demonstrations, and sells what they record as training data for physical AI. This is the whole loop, live on Monad testnet.
Thenar's arm is a six-axis robot that anyone can drive from a browser.
The hub lists open tasks. Each one is a bounty held in escrow in MON on Monad, and each accepted run is paid in the same transaction that records it.
At the station, the arm moves objects into a target circle. A trained policy is driving here, so this is a practice run.
When the object settles, the run is measured for placement, smoothness and time. A practice run is scored, and never submitted.
Robotics labs fund the bounties. A lab's budget sits in a Privy server wallet, with a Privy policy that only lets it escrow bounties in Thenar's contract on Monad, up to 0.1 MON a transaction.
We post a bounty of 0.004 MON for one run. Privy signs it under the policy, and the transaction is being confirmed on Monad now.
Monadscan shows it confirmed: the lab wallet paying 0.004 MON into the Thenar protocol contract.
Now we ask the same wallet to send 0.01 MON anywhere else. Privy's policy engine refuses, and nothing is signed.
The recordings are sold to AI agents. An agent asks for a task's data, and the server answers with HTTP 402, Payment Required, priced at one cent of USDC on Monad.
First, World AgentKit asks AgentBook on World Chain whether a verified human stands behind the agent. This agent is not registered, so it pays.
The agent signs a one cent USDC authorisation, and the Monad facilitator submits it and pays the gas. The transfer is being confirmed on Monad now.
On Monadscan, the facilitator's transaction moves one cent of USDC from the agent's wallet to the corpus treasury. The agent paid no gas.
Every sale is written to the SalesLog contract on Monad, with the SHA-256 of the exact file served. The agent hashed its own copy and asked the contract how many sales served those bytes.
Follow the value. A person's run is scored and paid in MON on Monad. An agent pays for the data in USDC on Monad. And the file's fingerprint lands in a contract only the seller can write to.
The corpus itself is shares on Monad: Thenar Robot Corpus. Only whitelisted addresses can hold them, and an address is whitelisted only after a World ID check of a live human.
Holders are paid from sales as dividends. The issuer now declares a dividend of 0.01 MON, escrowed in the contract. The transaction is being confirmed on Monad now.
Monadscan shows the declaration on the shares contract. The record date is fixed in advance, two minutes out, so the snapshot of who holds cannot be chosen afterwards.
Holding a share needs a place on the whitelist. The agent's wallet has none, so the contract itself refuses it, with Account Is Not In Control List.
These are the three transactions from this recording, all on Monad: the lab's bounty, the agent's data sale, and the dividend declaration.

The easy attack on a bounty market is one person with a hundred wallets. Thenar signs a run only after a World ID Selfie Check, one per human, bound to one wallet. In this recording, a wallet with no proof was refused before anything was paid.
And here is the Selfie Check done for real. The operator scans their face in World App, the proof comes back, and the wallet is cleared to record.
The contracts page lists every Thenar contract on Monad testnet, with its address, code size and balance read live from the chain.
The status page checks the live system every fifteen seconds: the verifier key, the contract, the database and the chain.
People record the data, Monad pays them in MON, agents buy it for USDC on Monad, and World keeps it to one person per set of runs. Thanks for watching Thenar.
